rationale: Both validate rolls and track completion correctly. B uses the classic, easy-to-verify design: it stores a flat slice of rolls, and Score is a single linear walk that applies the strike, spare and open-frame rules. Roll is an explicit, well-commented state machine with a single pinsRemaining check that covers every too-many-pins case, including the tenth-frame bonus rolls. A stores frames and relies on a trailing empty frame as a game-over sentinel. Its frameScore re-flattens every roll and recomputes the start offset for each frame, which is convoluted and quadratic, and its tenth-frame pin validation is split across special cases. B has more state fields, but its logic is clearer and more direct.
